purpose: C.9 Example 6 (retroactive tier cashback): highest_only tier resolution suppresses the lower tier entirely, and the surviving tier's activate_rule (application: retroactive) re-rates the WHOLE annual window, not just the months after crossing -- every month ends up at rate_3 (3%), none stay at base (1%) or land on rate_2 (2%).

assumptions.note: Grocery ticket 700: 700*0.03=21.00 lands on an exact multiple of Rs0.01 (also true at 1%/2%), so there is zero paisa floor loss at any of the three rates -- no rounding_estimated flag expected.

_hand_computation: Stage 3 (match), pre-activation: rate_2 and rate_3 both require_activation, so every month's Rs35,000 grocery binds only to base (1%).
Stage 4 (accrue), pre-activation: 35,000*0.01=Rs350.00/month * 12 = Rs4,200.00 (matches test_rule_activations.py's own unit-test assertion for this exact scenario).

Stage 6-7 (thresholds): basis=milestone_eligible_spend, ANNIV, tier_mode=highest_only. Cumulative grocery crosses tier 1 (Rs1,00,000) in month 3 (1,05,000) and tier 2 (Rs3,00,000) in month 9 (3,15,000) -- highest_only fires ONLY tier 2's payload (activate_rule rate_3, retroactive), suppressing tier 1's (rate_2) entirely -- rate_2 never activates at all.

apply_rule_activations: retroactive re-rates the WHOLE window_months (all 12), not just months after crossing -- every month's base binding is replaced by rate_3. 35,000*0.03=Rs1,050.00/month * 12 = Rs12,600.00 (cashback_inr, single route, ratio 1.0).

No caps on this card -> no-op. No milestone/benefit payloads (activate_rule contributes 0 to MilestoneValue, its effect is already inside the re-rated gross reward above). No waiver threshold -> fee is never waived, but annual_fee itself is Rs0 anyway.
Fees: joining_fee=0 (unset), annual_fee=0 -> steady_fee = 0*1.18 = Rs0.00. year1_fee = (0+0)*1.18 = Rs0.00.
NACV Year-1 = 12,600.00 - 0 (fee) = Rs12,600.00 (identical -- activate_rule's re-rating doesn't depend on year-mode, only condition:on_renewal grants do, and this card has none).
